title: Polyglot invoker resumable protocol and typed-envelope examples
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: produce a set of concrete SDK examples (TypeScript, Python, Go) and a short protocol spec that demonstrate a resumable sessioned invocation model for streaming LLM output + tool/function calling using typed envelopes. This ticket covers: 1) a lightweight wire contract for fragmenting large structured outputs into typed envelopes with reassembly metadata; 2) session resumption semantics (resume token, idempotency, replay bounds); 3) backpressure and client-side buffering recommendations for mobile/embedded SDKs; 4) canonical example implementations for ts/py/go that show progressive tool handshake, tool invocation, error semantics, and migration notes from legacy single-stream callbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc PR merged that defines typed-envelope fields: envelope_id, total_parts (optional), seq, fragment_type (partial/final/heartbeat), checksum, schema_id, session_token

Three example packages (TypeScript, Python, Go) in the examples/ directory demonstrating: negotiated tool handshake, streaming increments of structured output as envelopes, resumption from a resume_token, and graceful fallback to polling mode
Integration test harness that simulates mid-stream disconnect and verifies client rehydration using resume_token and idempotent replays
Migration guide doc that maps legacy callback patterns to the new sessioned-resumable API with code snippets and recommended deprecation schedule
Security review sign-off attached (KMS usage when session_token persisted)
tasks: Draft wire-protocol spec (first pass) and post to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Resumable+Invocation+Spec
Implement minimal server-side resume_token issuance in runtime dev cluster (feature-flagged)
Build TS/py/go example clients under sdk-examples/resumable-invoker/
Write integration tests that inject network failures and assert deterministic reassembly
Write migration guide and example PR to SDK repos showing adapter code
Run security review with infra-security and update KMS usage notes
decisions: Use a compact typed-envelope JSON envelope (not CBOR) for human readability in examples, with an opt-in binary variant for production performance
resume_token will be opaque to clients; server will encode replay window and last_seq handled
Client must persist resume_token and last_seq in durable storage only if using resume; otherwise use short-lived in-memory tokens for ephemeral sessions
Backpressure model: client advertises max_inflight_fragments; server will respect but still provide heartbeat fragments every 5s to keep connections alive
tradeoffs: JSON envelopes increase bandwidth (vs CBOR) but simplify debugging and adoption across languages
Opaque resume_token hides server policy but requires strong guarantees for idempotency in server retries
Adding resume increases runtime complexity (stateful) — feature-flag to limit customer exposure until monitored at scale
notes: Related runtime ticket: implement ephemeral session table with GC after 24h of inactivity
We should coordinate with console team for telemetry: new metrics resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, fragment_reassembly_latency
Consider offering a server-side 'compact mode' that switches to binary envelopes and snappy compression for Dedicated customers
Drafted initial schema registry entry idea: schema_id references JSON schema stored in catalog for structured outputs
qa_plan: Unit tests for envelope packing/unpacking across all three example SDKs
Fuzz test: random fragment drop/reorder up to 10% and assert deterministic reassembly
Integration: simulate mid-stream connection loss at seq N and resume from token verifying no duplication or missing fragments
Load test: verify heartbeat policy holds at 5000 concurrent resumable sessions per region
risks: State growth in runtime if many long-lived resume tokens are issued — mitigate via conservative TTL and GC
Client misuse of resume_token leading to duplicate tool side-effects — recommend idempotency keys in tool calls
Cross-language parity issues: Go example must match the async generator patterns used by TS/Py
migration_notes: Legacy SDKs that relied on a single streaming callback must implement an adapter that consumes envelopes and emits semantic events (tool_call, tool_result, partial_struct, final_struct)
Provide a code snippet in each language for an adapter wrapper that converts old onData callbacks to new envelope consumers
Deprecation plan: new sessioned API GA -> 3 month overlap -> deprecation warnings in logs for legacy endpoint usage
